channels.label: New photographs and a rewritten profile
channels.rationale: Listing quality is the cheapest lever a shelter controls.
channels.evidence_detail: Not measurable in this dataset. Austin's public export contains no photograph or listing field, so no effect is estimated and none is claimed.
channels.time_note: Assumed coordination time per animal, not time to place or treat.

channels.label: Place in a foster home
channels.rationale: Foster placement precedes adoption for a large share of Austin adoptions, especially for neonates.
channels.evidence_detail: Historical association in the 2013–2022 Austin archive, under the previous shelter system: 12,175 of 62,130 adoptions carried the Foster outcome subtype, and neonates reached 47.8 percent cumulative adoption incidence by day 90 against 21.4 percent by day 30. This describes a pathway that was common; it does not measure what recruiting a foster changes.
channels.time_note: Assumed coordination time per animal, not time to place or treat.

channels.label: Feature at a weekend adoption event
channels.rationale: Puts the animal in front of walk-in traffic it would not otherwise see.
channels.evidence_detail: Event participation is not recorded in the public export, so no effect is estimated.
channels.time_note: Assumed coordination time per animal, not time to place or treat.

channels.label: Medical or behaviour intervention
channels.rationale: Intake condition is one of the strongest measured predictors of a slow exit.
channels.evidence_detail: Historical association in the 2013–2022 archive: animals arriving injured reached 18.5 percent 30-day adoption incidence against 43.4 percent for animals arriving in normal condition (Cox hazard ratio 0.477). Intake condition predicts a slower exit; this is not a measurement of what treatment changes, and no medical action is prescribed here.
channels.time_note: Assumed coordination time per animal, not time to place or treat.

channels.label: Senior-focused outreach
channels.rationale: Senior animals are the slowest life stage in this dataset.
channels.evidence_detail: Historical association in the 2013–2022 archive: the senior band reached 17.8 percent cumulative adoption incidence by day 30 against 59.8 percent for puppies and kittens (Cox hazard ratio 0.425). Archive era; the current dashboard's twelve-month medians are a different cohort and metric and can disagree.
channels.time_note: Assumed coordination time per animal, not time to place or treat.

channels.label: Feature on social channels
channels.rationale: Extends reach beyond walk-in traffic at near zero marginal cost.
channels.evidence_detail: No reach or referral data is available in the public export, so no effect is estimated.
channels.time_note: Assumed coordination time per animal, not time to place or treat.
